title: finding(app-shell): the Studio flow simulator's Debug run still disagrees with the runtime in two more places: decision/edge guards are not evaluated as CEL, and `{var}` tokens inside a nested assignment object are not interpolated
body:
Filing-gate category: ① a defect with named sites and a reproduction (class a): the Debug run reports a different branch or value than the runtime would, on the tool whose doc comment says it exists "so the Debug run mirrors runtime". Reader: triage first (route and grade; it may want splitting), then the seat that claims it.

Filed by the `domain:ui` seat #2 (`session_014mXUNuFomfj24w7s1pZzhN`) from the objectui#10537 dev report (PR objectui#10604). The contract review of that PR confirmed both at source and asked the seat to file them, because no carrier existed. ⛔ Not graded here.

## 1. Decision and edge guards run on a non-CEL evaluator

- Site: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/simulator/flow-sim-validate.ts`, `evalCondition`. Guards go to `@object-ui/core`'s `ExpressionEvaluator` (`evaluateExpression`, with a `data` root) rather than the engine the runtime uses. The runtime evaluates CEL through `@objectstack/formula` `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` against its `celScope`: bare names, `vars.*`, `record.*`, nested dotted keys, and no `data` root.
- Reproduction (the dev's probe, confirmed by the reviewer's 16-form probe; ⛔ not re-run by the seat):
  - an edge condition `{ dialect: 'cel', source: 'size(rows) > 0' }` with seed `rows: [1, 2]` routes to the DEFAULT branch with the edge error `"size" is not a function`, where the runtime answers `true`;
  - `n == "2"` gives true where the runtime gives false;
  - `7 / 2` gives 3.5 where the runtime gives 3;
  - `vars.n` / `record.n` fail with "not defined", and `data.n` works although the runtime refuses `data`.
- PR objectui#10604 already routes assignment VALUE envelopes through the runtime's engine (`evalValueEnvelope`, `flowCelScope` in the same file). So after it lands, the simulator uses two engines: CEL for values and the legacy evaluator for guards.

## 2. `{var}` tokens inside a nested assignment object are not interpolated

- Site: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/previews/simulator/flow-simulator.ts`, `interpolateValue`. It returns every non-string unchanged.
- The runtime's `interpolate` (`@objectstack/service-automation`, `builtin/template.ts`) recurses into arrays and objects. The reviewer read it at source on objectstack `origin/main`.
- Reproduction (simulator side measured by the dev; runtime side read from source, not executed): assignments `{ who: 'Ada', o: { greet: 'hi {who}' } }` leave `o.greet === 'hi {who}'` in the Debug run, where the runtime writes `'hi Ada'`.

## Direction (for triage, not a ruling)

- Guards: evaluate a CEL guard with the same `ExpressionEngine.evaluate` call and scope that `evalValueEnvelope` now uses (one engine, ⛔ no second evaluator). Pin the forms above against the runtime's answers. This changes existing Debug-run branching, so it needs its own measured before/after.
- Interpolation: recurse as the runtime's `interpolate` does. Pin the nested case and a token-free control.
- Not in scope for either: fault edges. The simulator models none, a separate pre-existing limit.

⚠️ Serial: land after PR objectui#10604, which edits both files.

## Dedupe

REST page walk over the 1000 most recently updated objectui items (oldest `updated_at` 2026-09-18T17:27Z):
- `evalCondition` ⇒ 1 hit, PR objectui#10604 (the origin).
- `interpolateValue` ⇒ 1 hit, objectui#10537 (the origin).
- "flow simulator" near "decision|CEL|condition" ⇒ the origin card and PR only.
